summary: Every captured argument must be classified as fixed or placeholder and every unused call-time argument must be forwarded, giving a linear lower bound that the accepted one-pass merge matches.

optimality.argument: A correct wrapper must inspect all a captured entries because any one may be a placeholder, and in the zero-placeholder case it must forward all r call-time values. Thus the worst case requires Omega(a + r) work. The accepted source scans args once, consumes each replacement once, and appends the remaining restArgs suffix once, establishing O(a + r).

replacement_checks.evidence: Skipping a captured position can miss a placeholder, while skipping an unused call-time position changes the required argument list.
Two monotone indices visit each captured and call-time entry at most once before one target invocation.
Node regression covers every authored case, wrapper reuse without captured-array mutation, receiver forwarding, and independently maximal captured and call-time array lengths.
